title: AWS Bedrock (LLM)
description: Models on AWS Bedrock as an LLM tier, through gohort's Bedrock client, signed with an AWS credential that signs as this machine: its profile, SSO session or environment.
setup_notes: By default it signs as this machine's AWS identity, so set that up first: aws configure, or aws sso login for SSO, under the AWS profile set for it (blank uses $AWS_PROFILE, then the default chain). It needs bedrock:InvokeModel (bedrock-mantle:CreateInference for the Messages API), and the model enabled in the region. To sign with an access key pair instead, give ACCESS_KEY_ID:SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as its AWS key pair. gohort provides one, named bedrock and listed as AWS Bedrock; another, with its own key, is added from here. Choose it under Admin > LLMs > Worker LLM (or Lead LLM), where its region, API and key are set and the tier names its model; Test connection there makes one short real chat. Converse speaks to any Bedrock model; the Messages API and InvokeModel to Claude only. Many accounts must call newer models through an inference profile: name the model as us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 rather than the bare id. Add per_million_input and per_million_output to the spec's cost to price its tokens.

questions.name: name
questions.label: Connector name
questions.help: Lowercase letters, digits, dashes and underscores; the LLM settings list it by this name.

config.name: region
config.label: AWS region
config.help: Where the model runs, such as us-east-1 or us-west-2.

config.name: api
config.label: Bedrock API
config.help: Which Bedrock API your AWS role may call. All three stream.

config.name: profile
config.label: AWS profile
config.help: Which of this machine's AWS profiles to sign as. Blank uses $AWS_PROFILE, then the default chain.

config.name: aws_keys
config.label: AWS key pair
config.help: Blank signs as this machine, with its own AWS identity (its profile, SSO session or environment).
config.detail: Or give an access key pair as ACCESS_KEY_ID:SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. Signing as this machine needs bedrock:InvokeModel for the model in the region, and, for SSO, aws sso login on this machine under the profile.
